newsitem.title: GREECE: Greece draws U.S. anger over convicted guerrilla.
newsitem.headline: Greece draws U.S. anger over convicted guerrilla.

text.p: The United States on Wednesday criticised Greece after an Athens court reduced the jail term of a man convicted of the 1982 bombing of a Pan American World Airways airliner and said he should be freed for good behaviour.
"We believe that convicted terrorists should serve their (full) term," a U.S. embassy spokesman said.
Washington is expected to put pressure on Athens to try to have the decision in the case of Mohammed Rashid, 46, reversed.
"The court council has ruled in accordance with existing laws," government spokesman Dimitris Reppas said. He did not elaborate.
Rashid's lawyer, Spyros Fitrakis, said a three-member court accepted on Tuesday an appeal by Rashid to be freed after serving more than half of his 15-year sentence and be expelled from Greece.
"The court ruled in favour of our appeal. He will be out in a few days," Fitrakis told Reuters.

Rashid was arrested at Athens airport in May 1988 after a tip-off by U.S. authorities. Greece rejected a U.S. extradiction request and put him on trial in Athens, a decision which became a test-case for U.S.-Greek relations.
Rashid was found guilty of premeditated murder for planting a bomb on a Pan Am airliner in 1982. A Japanese teenager was killed and 15 other passengers were wounded. The plane landed in Hawaii.

The self-avowed officer in the Palestinian Liberation Organisation (PLO) said throughout that he was the victim of mistaken identity. He was sentenced to 18 years by an Athens court in 1992 but later had his sentence reduced to 15 years.

"We are happy that this injustice is finally over," an official of PLO's diplomatic representation in Athens said. "Our justice minister talked with the Greek justice minister to arrange the details of the expulsion."
Rashid wants to go to the new Palestinian entity but the PLO official said this may be difficult.

"Our borders are still controlled by the Israelis. If he tries to go to Palestine he may be picked up by the (Israeli) security forces and handed over to the Americans. We are also looking for another country that will temporarily accept him."
